messages:
Alex: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-picker rollout p95 decode latency on host proxy is up ~12% on our small-req workload. noticed spike around request parsing tokenization stage. :grimacing:
Sara: ugh. seen anything in traces?
Alex: trace snippets attached in prod traces but quick grep shows hot path in native tokenizer: `tokenizer::scan_chars` and `parse_request_proto` dominating CPU. perf top snapshot: `tokenizer::scan_chars (32%)`, `grpc::writev_serialize (10%)`, `kvcache::lookup (8%)`.
Jamal: can you paste the perf flame? also which kernel-picker config did we flip?
Alex: we flipped `kernel_picker.mode = heuristic_v2` and lowered `host_preparse_budget_ms` from 6 -> 3 in the rollout.
Sara: that budget drop was to tighten latency tail with batching, hmm. could be preparse starving CPU and increasing fragmentation in streaming writev.
Chris: I ran a quick pprof on canary: stack shows repeated short-lived allocations in tokenizer buffer resize during stream chunking. lots of small writes => poor writev coalescing over HTTP2.
Irene: infra-bot FYI: observed increased small-write ratio on ingress for canary group between 02:10-03:00 UTC.
infra-bot: alert: canary group 7 — small_write_pct increased from 18% -> 41% (source: ingress-metrics).
Alex: logs: sample span:
```
[2026-03-22T02:14:11Z] req=abcd parse_ms=2 decode_ms=6 token_scan_us=1200 kv_lookup_us=80 writev_calls=4 total_ms=18
[2026-03-22T02:14:12Z] req=abce parse_ms=1 decode_ms=12 token_scan_us=3200 kv_lookup_us=90 writev_calls=7 total_ms=27
```
Sara: big variance in token_scan_us. looks like some inputs are hitting the slowpath. any change to tokenizer lexicon or UTF8 path?
Jamal: nothing intentional. but heuristic_v2 also changes per-req kernel selection which can change sequence-length handling and therefore cache pressure. Might be kvcache churn.
Chris: kvcache metrics show increased eviction rate on canary. kv-hit dropped 0.94 -> 0.86 on hot prefix workload. evict rate doubled.
Irene: suggestion: revert `host_preparse_budget_ms` to 6 for canary and re-evaluate; also try disabling `heuristic_v2` on a subset to isolate.
Alex: agreed. quick repro plan:
- revert budget -> baseline
- run microbench (small-req, seq=32/64 mix) with `kernel_picker=heuristic_v1` and `heuristic_v2`
- gather perf (perf record + pprof) and ingress writev metrics
Sara: also run with `batcher.max_batch_size=4` vs 8 to see batching heuristics interaction. last rollout tightened batching and might increase preparse tail.
Jamal: I'll run tests. scheduling now. command I will run:
```
./benchctl run --suite smallreq-mix --kernel-picker v1,v2 --batch-sizes 4,8 --preparse-budget 3,6 --measure perf,pprof,kvstats
```
Chris: when you run, include `--capture tcpdump` for 5s sample to inspect HTTP2 frame sizes. fragmentation might explain extra writev calls.
Jamal: noted. starting runs; will post results in this thread. ETA ~45m.
perf-bot: perf job queued: smallreq-mix (v1,v2) — job id 9582.
Sara: if we confirm kvcache thrash + tokenizer slowpath, we should bump preparse budget and add a small pooling buffer to tokenizer to avoid repeated allocations (low-effort microfix).
Alex: agree, low-risk mitigation: bump budget and add pooling; longer term we should look at kernel-picker heuristics to avoid switching kernel variants for very short sequences (that's amplifying allocations).
Irene: also add a short kvcache TTL bump for hot prefixes (e.g., 2s -> 5s) as an experiment to reduce eviction churn during bursts.
Jamal: first run finished — quick summary:
- v2 + budget=3 + batch=8: p95 +12% (matches prod)
- v1 + budget=3 + batch=8: p95 +3%
- v2 + budget=6 + batch=8: p95 +4%
- v2 + budget=3 + batch=4: p95 +1%
Irene: that matrix suggests the budget change is the biggest lever, batching interacts too.
Chris: perf flame for v2+budget=3 shows tokenizer alloc spikes and `grpc::frame_writev` more frequent. tcpdump shows many ~1-2KB frames instead of coalesced 8-12KB.
Sara: actionable: rollback budget to 6 for rollout, keep kernel_picker=heuristic_v2 but add a guard: if seq_len < 64 prefer v1 kernel (or do not reselect). also tune batcher to prefer slightly smaller batch size for tail-sensitive routes.
Alex: created PR: `rollout/host-preparse-budget-rollback` (link: https://git.internal/r/rollout/1234) — will patch canary and monitor.
Jamal: opened perf run ticket with full artifacts (pprof flamegraphs, tcpdump) — ticket #INF-762. attaching link.
perf-bot: job 9582 complete. artifacts: https://perf.internal/artifacts/9582.zip
Irene: monitoring shows canary p95 back to baseline after budget rollback patch applied to canary group. small_write_pct dropped back to 20%. kv-hit recovered to 0.93.
Alex: great work. follow-ups:
- Jamal: add tokenizer buffer pool PR (small, low-risk) — target: next week
- Chris: add kernel-picker guard for small sequences
- Sara/Irene: run more A/B with batch sizes across 3 different client mixes
All: add results to the postmortem doc (link in #eng-runtime). :thumbsup:
